content.title: About
content.content: Vanilla ice cream is a frozen dessert made from milk, cream, and natural vanilla flavoring. It features a smooth, creamy texture with the characteristic sweet aroma of vanilla.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Vanilla ice cream became a classic flavor in the United States in the early 20th century.
Traditional flavor comes from vanilla beans, but most commercial production uses synthetic vanillin.
Ice cream is stored at about ‑18 °C (0 °F) to maintain its structure and taste.
Slow freezing creates smaller ice crystals, enhancing the vanilla flavor.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: The dairy base provides calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Milk and cream supply riboflavin (B2) and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: Carbohydrates and fats give a rapid source of energy.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of cavities.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience digestive discomfort.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: Allergy to milk or cream requires complete avoidance of ice cream.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve ice cream in cups, cones, or bowls; it pairs well with fruit, berries, nuts, sauces, and baked goods.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep ice cream in a freezer at ‑18 °C or lower. After opening, consume within 1–2 weeks to prevent ice crystal formation.
